category: X6-F4 Open-set and out-of-distribution road objects
title: Beyond Pixel Uncertainty: Bounding the OoD Objects in Road Scenes
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
key_idea: Turns pixel-level OoD scores into object-level boxes: an open-world detector finds all objects, in-distribution boxes are suppressed, and the remaining OoD proposals prune false positives or prompt a box-based segmenter.
method: Detector with universal queries plus in-distribution-enhanced NMS; DetSeg-R refines existing anomaly maps, DetSeg-S uses a box-prompted segmenter; vanishing-point guided Hungarian matching smooths predictions within a video clip.
data: Benchmarks not named in the abstract; a third-party summary page lists RoadAnomaly, Fishyscapes, SegmentMeIfYouCan and LostAndFound (UNVERIFIED).
reported_result: Abstract: reduces the FPR95 of previous methods by up to 37.45%.
relation_to_project: Owner deck lead (ICCV 2025) confirmed. Shows object-level reasoning plus temporal smoothing cuts the false positives of pixel-uncertainty scores, a pattern for the benign or unknown branch. Not an attack detector; a large open-world detector, not lightweight.
notes: ICCV 2025 pp. 8472-8481 per the CVF open-access page; Crossref record matches. Metrics are pixel-level OoD measures (FPR95, AP), not detection operating points.

category: X6-F1 Calibration of object detectors
title: Towards Building Self-Aware Object Detectors via Reliable Uncertainty Quantification and Calibration
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
key_idea: Self-aware object detection task: a detector must accept or reject a whole image from image-level uncertainty, give detection confidences calibrated for both classification and localisation (LaECE), and stay robust to domain shift.
method: Image-level uncertainty from the most confident detections, reject threshold set with a pseudo-OOD set; per-class post-hoc calibrators; Detection Awareness Quality (DAQ) joins accuracy, calibration and image rejection.
data: Two use cases, one for autonomous driving; per use case 45K in-distribution, 110K OOD and 3 x 45K corrupted domain-shift test images (CVPR slides).
reported_result: Paper text: detectors turn out to be strong image-level OOD detectors. A figure shows LaECE 43.3% for a base model and 17.7% after linear-regression calibration; slides state LaECE of about 10-20% for the tested detectors.
relation_to_project: Closest template for the abstain branch of all five slides: an explicit image-level reject plus calibrated detections, evaluated together under shift. Rejects whole images, not single objects; no attacks; no three-way output.
notes: Crossref record matches. arXiv id read on the arXiv page in a search result (arXiv API not called: host stopped). Numbers come from a figure caption and the CVPR slides seen in search results.

category: X6-F1 Calibration of object detectors
title: On Calibration of Object Detectors: Pitfalls, Evaluation and Baselines
venue: European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2024), LNCS 15079
key_idea: Shows that common detector calibration evaluation (D-ECE with AP, temperature scaling) misleads; proposes joint evaluation with LaECE0, LaACE0 and LRP at tuned thresholds, plus post-hoc Platt scaling and isotonic regression for detectors.
method: Per-class thresholds cross-validated with LRP, then per-class post-hoc calibrators fitted on a held-out validation set; calibration errors align confidence with IoU to the matched ground truth.
data: COCO and LVIS mini test splits plus corrupted domain-shift versions (COCO minitest-C, LVIS minitest-C), per the paper and supplement extracts.
reported_result: Abstract: D-DETR with post-hoc isotonic regression beats the train-time method Cal-DETR by more than 7 D-ECE on COCO; properly evaluated post-hoc calibrators are cheaper and more effective than train-time calibration.
relation_to_project: Supports a cheap post-hoc calibrator on a frozen detector (all slides freeze the detector) and warns that D-ECE plus AP comparisons can mislead. Calibrates to IoU, not to attack probability.

venue: The Annals of Statistics

category: X6-F1 Calibration of object detectors
title: Multivariate Confidence Calibration for Object Detection
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
key_idea: Calibrates detector confidence jointly with box position and scale from the regression branch and introduces the detection expected calibration error (D-ECE), showing miscalibration depends on object location.
method: Box-sensitive (multivariate) post-hoc calibration in a black-box setting with precision as the accuracy surrogate; D-ECE binned over confidence and box properties.
reported_result: Figure caption: miscalibration on COCO rises as predictions approach the image borders. Abstract: the methods beat standard calibration models across locations and scales; no numbers in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Origin of D-ECE, the measure most detector-calibration papers report; shows calibration should be conditioned on where and how large the object is, which matters for small, distant signs. P2-P1503 criticises D-ECE-based evaluation.

category: X6-F1 Calibration of object detectors
title: Bridging Precision and Confidence: A Train-Time Loss for Calibrating Object Detection
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
key_idea: Auxiliary train-time loss that aligns the class confidence of boxes with their precision, through a differentiable proxy of minibatch true and false positive counts, to reduce calibration error in and out of domain.
method: BPC loss added to the detector training loss; evaluated with D-ECE on in-domain and out-of-domain splits.
data: Six benchmark datasets including MS-COCO, Cityscapes, Sim10k and BDD100k (abstract); Foggy Cityscapes and a corrupted COCO (CorCOCO) as out-of-domain sets (paper figure and code README).
reported_result: Abstract: lower calibration error than strong calibration baselines in and out of domain. Code README table (D-DETR): D-ECE 12.8 to 10.3 on MS-COCO and 10.8 to 9.4 on CorCOCO, while temperature scaling raised D-ECE to 14.2 and 12.3.
relation_to_project: Evidence that detector calibration error changes under domain shift (fog, corruption), the condition of slides 02 to 04 at night or in weather. Needs detector retraining, which conflicts with the frozen-detector design; P2-P1503 reports post-hoc calibrators beating train-time losses.

category: X6-F2 Selective prediction, abstention and reject options
title: Two Coupled Rejection Metrics Can Tell Adversarial Examples Apart
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
key_idea: Adds a reject option to adversarially trained classifiers: confidence and a learned rectified confidence (R-Con) form two coupled rejection metrics that provably separate correctly from wrongly classified inputs.
method: Rectified rejection head sharing the backbone, trained with binary cross-entropy to predict true-label confidence; evaluated by accuracy at a fixed true positive rate and ROC-AUC, including adaptive attacks.
reported_result: Abstract: the module improves robustness across adversarial training frameworks with little extra computation. Paper table 1: an adversarially trained ResNet-18 scores 53.58% on PGD-10 inputs, 57.23% on inputs kept by a confidence rejector at 95% true positive rate, and 88.75% with the true-label-confidence oracle.
relation_to_project: Shows how to evaluate an abstain head at a fixed operating point and against adaptive attackers, and how far plain confidence is from an ideal rejector. Digital perturbations on small classifiers, not physical attacks on detectors.
code_or_data: github.com/P2333/Rectified-Rejection (named in the arXiv version) UNVERIFIED
notes: Crossref record matches. Table numbers read in the arXiv HTML extract in a search result.

title: Adaptive Bounding Box Uncertainties via Two-Step Conformal Prediction
venue: European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2024), LNCS 15146
key_idea: Two-step conformal procedure for multi-object detection: a conformal class-label set first, then box intervals that carry the label uncertainty, so coverage also holds for misclassified objects; ensemble and quantile variants adapt to object size.
method: Class-conditional split conformal prediction for labels, then for box coordinates (Box-Std, Box-Ens, Box-CQR), on pretrained black-box detectors.

category: X6-F4 Open-set and out-of-distribution road objects
title: The Overlooked Elephant of Object Detection: Open Set
venue: IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
key_idea: Formalises open-set object detection: unknown objects are often detected as known classes with very high confidence; proposes an open-set evaluation protocol and a metric (wilderness impact) for how unknowns degrade precision.
method: Open-set protocol with detectors trained on PASCAL VOC and tested with unknown objects; precision under growing shares of unknown samples.
data: PASCAL VOC and MS-COCO (abstract and paper extract).
reported_result: Figure caption: single-shot detectors (RetinaNet, YOLOv2) lose more than Faster R-CNN when unknowns are present, and the dropout-sampling approach gave much worse results.
relation_to_project: Confidence alone cannot separate known from unknown objects: high-confidence false detections occur without any attack, so an attack flag needs evidence beyond the score. Supports benign look-alike testing.
notes: Crossref record matches. Abstract and a figure caption read on the CVF page.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017)
key_idea: Builds a selective classifier on a trained network that rejects inputs as needed to guarantee a user-chosen risk with high probability while maximising coverage; frames performance as a risk-coverage curve.
